quest.title: Shimmering Memories
quest.description: One day, you are stopped by a familiar voice while in the Court of Fontaine...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Go to the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Stocking up on materials, confirming construction timelines, discussing compensation terms with families affected by the disaster... Between all of that, I've been making a lot of trips between the Court and Poisson.

choices.text: Wasn't Spina di Rosula affected, too?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, though the victims have received relief payments from the Court, in my opinion, as the administrators of Poisson, Spina di Rosula should take some responsibility as well.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Our financial situation right now isn't the best, so all we've been doing is signing agreements for the damages to be repaid at a later date.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Though just pieces of paper now, they demonstrate our commitment. They're necessary to restore the people's faith in us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, spoken like a true President... You are a really responsible leader! That must be taking up most of your time though, right?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, you bet. Between that and all the other errands I have to run at the Court, I'm always forgetting one thing or another.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So before I came over this time, I took a page from Melus' book and decided to make a list of everything. This way, it's easy to see which tasks you haven't checked off.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And then...?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And then... Since Melus loved using shorthand, I decided to also follow his example, and come up with some shorthand of my own.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But after running a few errands in the city, I'm kind of struggling to even read my own handwriting anymore, hehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That does sound like you all right... So what kind of shorthand did you use?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Want to take a look?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... Wait, there's nothing here but a bunch of weird symbols!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This looks like... a piece of kelp wrapped around a stick? And this other one... Um, is it supposed to be a boar in a box?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hmm... The first one has to do with confirming the final payment amount for the fishermen, while the second one is a reminder to try the new burger that just hit the market!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon can definitely see how you might forget what each of these means!

choices.text: Maybe just use standardized shorthand symbols next time?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, thank you for your advice. These are the kinds of things you only really figure out once you've tried them out yourself.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I thought that as long as I understood my shorthand when I came up with it, I'd be sure to remember the symbols when I looked at them later. Unfortunately, I've definitely proven myself wrong...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, now you know for next time!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, I should have already taken care of most of the things on the list. There are still a few symbols that I can't decipher, but... I don't think they're anything too super important.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Worse comes to worst, I'll just make another trip.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so you're going to head back now?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yep, that's the plan. Oh, actually, since we talked about the reconstruction earlier, wanna come with me and check out the town for yourself?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You said you don't have any plans, right? So we can just catch a boat and head over. It won't take long at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh, it's a bit sudden... But Paimon doesn't see why not! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I'd be interested in taking a look.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Then let's go. We'll take a boat over.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you mean the aquabus, right? Like the Clementine Line!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, sorry, I meant our own boat. The aquabus doesn't have a station near Poisson, so we'll use one of the Spina's boats.

choices.text: <color=#FFC300FF>Sure, sounds good to me.</color>

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, follow me. I'll take you there.

choices.text: I've still got something to do, so why don't you head over there first?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, sure, that sounds fine to me. Just so happens I wanted to check some of the equipment on the boat as well. Just find me by the water when you're ready!

choices.text: It would be a pretty nice break, too.
Maybe just write out each item next time?
Should you really be the ones offering compensation?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The engineer is still doing a few routine safety checks. We can head out as soon as we get the green light!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Paimon has always wanted to ask... The three aquabus lines are all named after people in your family, right?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right. Callas and Navia are self-explanatory, while Clementine was the name that my mother went by.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Spina di Rosula was one of the main sponsors for the construction, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you provided the Mora to build the lines, then why isn't there even a dedicated line to Poisson?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Spina di Rosula built all the lines, yet you still have to take a special boat just to go home... Paimon doesn't get it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, what I heard is that most of our businesses don't actually use Poisson as a hub, so there was no real reason to build a line straight to Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You are right that it is a bit strange, though. If you've already committed to build three lines, why not just add a fourth?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's what Paimon's saying! The aquabus is so convenient, it's really a huge shame.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, it is what it is. You know what my father was like — even I often struggled to figure out what was going on in his head.

choices.text: Well, something that big also wouldn't have been just his call.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, but that would only be the case if he cared about what others thought. My father was always really stubborn. Once he made up his mind, good luck getting him to change it.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: From what I've heard, the rights of all the other members of the Spina only went as far as giving him advice or suggestions, and no further. That included my mother, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Well, that explains why you weren't on the greatest of terms with him.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah, because I wouldn't just let him keep getting his way! He was just... *sigh* not very agreeable.

response.speaker: Leslie
response.text: Boss, the boat's ready! We can head out.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, then let's head out!

choices.text: Perhaps the rest of the Spina didn't see a point to having a fourth line?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It'll be a while before we get to Poisson. Let's keep talking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Navia, what was your mother like as a person?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon's sorry, she totally forgot that you mentioned before that she passed away during childbirth, so you probably don't remember her at all...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that's alright! I've heard many stories about her from the rest of the Spina. They've always said that they were sure we would have gotten along famously.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: While my papa was stiff like a board, my mother was supposedly super cheerful and funny. Their complementary personalities allowed them to make up for each other's flaws.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: My father would run the businesses and expand our reach, while my mother would keep the peace and make sure that everyone was happy. Their work made sure that the Spina could grow and thrive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like they were not just a well-matched couple, but fantastic business partners as well!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah, but those are just stories and anecdotes after all. It's hard for me to piece together a more complete or intimate picture of her.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But sometimes, I'd still look at the Clementine Line and wonder... Would the Spina and Poisson still be what they are today, had my mother survived?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Silver once said that a name is a kind of inscription — a way to etch a memory into the world. When given a name, a cold, inanimate object can gain a completely new meaning.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So, I will always associate the Line with her in my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Over the past few weeks, I've also begun to appreciate how water can take in and hold our most intense feelings and memories, as well as how one may reflect on their past by watching the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I've lost many beloved people and memories to the sea. Even though I cannot stop for them, and must continue to keep moving...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The fact won't change that they existed in my life, and gave me the reason and motivation to move forward.

choices.text: Do you miss them?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Always, but no matter what, we can't change the past.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But I tell myself that I need to keep looking towards the future. Everyone, even my parents, have all already overcome so many obstacles.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Besides, I'm the President of Spina di Rosula. I've got to keep my chin up.

choices.text: Missing Melus and Silver?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Of course. I still haven't really gotten used to a life without them...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We've reached the shore. Let's go — I'll show you the new Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia... Do you think she's doing alright?

choices.text: She seems to be managing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon supposes you're right... She's really been through a lot. It couldn't have been easy, shouldering so much by herself...

choices.text: She's always been having to cope with one thing or another.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Navia, Florent! Guess who's back!

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Huh!? But aren't you supposed to...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, well if it isn't Colter! Back already from the Fortress of Meropide?

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that's right! I've finally finished serving my time. Gotta say, turns out I was a lot tougher than I thought!

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: After I got out, I immediately made a beeline back to Poisson. You could say that familiar briny smell became a primal call, urging me to forget everything else and just come back home.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: You wouldn't believe how much I've missed Melissa's Grilled Fish — I dreamed about it every time I had to get a Welfare Meal down there underneath the sea!

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: It's good to have you back, Colter. You look as well as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And this guy is...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah, let me introduce you. This is Colter, another of Spina di Rosula's members. He was found guilty and sentenced to the Fortress of Meropide some time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But looking at it now, it was probably another one of Marcel's plots while he worked at the Confrerie of Cabriere.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Wait, wait, Mr. Marcel? What do you mean, he was involved in some sort of plot?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Have you not heard anything at all about the "Water from the Primordial Sea" case?

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Well, I know that Fontaine got flooded, but then the water levels miraculously receded. I thought that was all there was to it, and didn't care to ask for any more details. Do you mean... Mr. Marcel was somehow involved with all of that?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Looks like we'll have to explain everything from the top. That case... A lot of things have happened in Poisson since then.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: First things first, let me introduce you to these two. They're my most trusted partners, and they've been with me through thick and thin. Now, you could call them Spina di Rosula's VIP helpers.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Oh, nice to meet you! I don't recall Navia ever generously complimenting anyone like that before, so you must be pretty amazing to get that from her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, yeah, we are indeed pretty amazing, but we've been cool since before we even met her!

choices.text: We just followed Navia's lead.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Humble again as always, I see, even when I was totally sincere with my praise.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Nice, nice. Spina di Rosula always seems to attract great people.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Oh, that reminds me — where are Melus and Silver? Aren't they always by your side?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Um... About that...

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Colter, a lot of things happened while you were gone. As you can see, even Poisson isn't quite the same as... how it was before you left.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: They lost their lives keeping me safe during the flood.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: ...What did you say?

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: This isn't some kind of morbid welcome-home prank, right? You're just scaring me on purpose, because I don't know anything about what's happened...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'm sorry, but it's the truth. They weren't the only people we lost, either. Many others, including Melissa, also lost their lives in the disaster.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Melus, and Melissa... Dead? They're just... gone?

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Melus... I was planning to give him a surprise gift once I ran into him again in town. Ah, I can't believe it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey, keep it together...

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Melus and Colter were friends for many years, and even served on many missions together during the early days of the Spina. I can understand how he feels.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Let's sit down somewhere, so I can tell you everything that has happened while you were gone. Fair warning, there was... a lot.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I... Okay.

choices.text: All credit to Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, now you suddenly resist taking a dig at Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Navia explains everything that has happened recently to Colter.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: All of this... It's unbelievable... I can't believe that those stories were real, it all really happened. Has the world gone mad?

choices.text: Had I not personally experienced all those events...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I think you and I both feel the same way about the profound tragedy of Melus's loss, and... the sheer depravity of Marcel's actions.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I thought Mr. Marcel would always stand by the Spina... Everything he had, the Spina gave to him.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: It's unconscionable to have received all that, and yet still plot to kidnap and dissolve you for his insane research.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: The good news is that the Confrerie of Cabriere is no more. Gone with them, too, is the entire Sinthe manufacturing and distribution network.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: We've finally closed the curtain on that long struggle.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Are you sure? But if Marcel wanted to rebel against us, he probably sent word in secret to Romeuf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Romewho?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Not a name I've heard before, either.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Florent should remember him. You see, there was once a major internal dispute regarding funding the construction of the aquabus lines.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Romeuf was the leader of the faction that thought such a vast sum of Mora would be better spent improving the town of Poisson.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: But Mr. Callas believed that an opportunity to collaborate with the Court of Fontaine and the Fontaine Research Institute was hard to come by, and would allow us to build many valuable relationships.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Not only would the aquabus be a good business investment, it would also boost our reputation among the general populace, eventually paying us massive dividends down the line.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: But the two couldn't come to an agreement. Romeuf ended up taking a lot of people with him when he left Spina di Rosula altogether, and the split was on extremely bad terms.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ugh, and with Papa's stubbornness, I can definitely imagine how it must have gone down...

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: And, of course, when he was suffering the slings and arrows of outrageous injustice... Those "relationships" that he spent a fortune to build didn't help in the least.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Yeah... You could say it was the price he paid for sticking to his beliefs.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That couldn't have been the first time a dispute like that happened, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's a good point! If Callas was really as stubborn as you say, then wouldn't he have argued with the rank and file all the time?

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Oh yeah, it eventually became a thing that just happened on every day that ended with "y." But, Navia... I mean, Boss, you might not know this, but he wasn't always like that.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: He used to be a lot better with taking counsel. With him listening to our advice, and Ms. Clementine also frequently on our side, it was pretty smooth sailing for a good many years.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: But on the matter of the aquabus, even Ms. Clementine completely stood by Mr. Callas' side.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Huh, I never knew... But from my perspective, Romeuf's position had a lot going for it. Couldn't they have sat down and talked it out?

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: I think the aquabus was just the straw that broke the camel's back. On that topic, they eventually came to a rather... radical conclusion.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: They believed that... Ms. Clementine lost her ability to serve as an impartial mediator when she became pregnant with Callas' child.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So... they thought she had betrayed them?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But that doesn't make any sense. Before she was their mediator, my mother was also her own person and a member of the Spina. She should have the right to take any side she wished.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Yeah, but to them, even taking a side was betrayal enough. They felt like their voices could no longer be heard once their sole mediator had gone over to the other side.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Of course, Ms. Clementine then passed away, and Mr. Callas began to regard the completion of the aquabus project as her final wish. With that, the last hope of reconciliation was gone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what happened...

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: From that point on, Romeuf and his people cut ties with the Spina, and never gave us any kind of professional or personal courtesy ever again.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Perhaps they've regarded us as enemies ever since they left. But even so, there is still no proof that they ever acted in concert with Marcel.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I've also heard that they aren't in a good financial position, so they've been lying low for a while. But as long as they exist, they'll continue to be a threat.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I think Colter's got a point. Both Marcel and Romeuf had my father in their sights for a very long time.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Even though Marcel's faction has been dissolved, we still don't know anything about Romeuf's whereabouts. If they're still trying to get revenge on us...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...With how distracted and vulnerable we are, now would be the best time.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Good thinking, Boss. We should keep an eye on them at all times. I'll let my men know right away.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Mhm, thank you for that, Florent. And Colter, thank you for telling me about this as well.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Don't worry, it's nothing. Do you have a moment right now? How about we go out for a walk?

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I've heard so many incredulous things today... I'm finding it a bit hard to calm down, even now. I mean, to think that I'll just... never see them again...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: In that case, why don't we go back to the Court? I can pick up Adele's uniform while we're there as well. It'll save Florent's guys a trip.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Want to come with me again, you two? You don't mind, do you, Colter?

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: O—Oh, of course, that's fine by me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's go! Paimon feels like a lot's hinging on this visit.

choices.text: We want to see Adele cheer up.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, we really are the best of partners. Come on, let's go.

choices.text: We want to see the future star of the Spina.
I would also have found them very difficult to accept.

talks.objective: Relax with Colter as you head to the Court of Fontaine
Relax with Colter as you head to the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, we've walked far enough for now. Let's take a break!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Since we're out for a walk, we shouldn't stress too much about the destination.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Hehe, I've grown old, so I'm not as fit as before. It's a good thing that at least my work down in the Fortress was quite the workout.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon thinks you're doing great! We didn't have to slow down for you at all.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Back in the days before the aquabus lines were built, we often had to hike north with our goods, then catch a boat to the Court.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Melus and I must have traveled this way hundreds of times. When we were tired, we would lay down for a while on the grass, and when we were hungry, we'd catch a fish or two.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: The Spina was still on the rise back then. Mr. Callas was generous, and everyone had the chance to strike it rich. So of course, we all worked really hard.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: And now, in the blink of an eye, the aquabus lines have been built, and this road has fallen into disuse.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't really think that's a bad thing, though.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Oh, I know. I was just being a little nostalgic.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Then let's stay here a bit longer. Anyone want snacks?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Is this another chance to try some of Navia's macarons? Paimon's been dreaming of them!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hahaha, yep! I figured you wouldn't say no to a few more.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, wait, let me check if I have all the ingredients... *sigh* Melus and Silver used to take care of tasks like this.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Okay, the stove's looking good, and as for the ingredients...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Seems like we're all out of flour and sugar. The two most important ingredients of all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should I go get some?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, would you? But it would be too much to ask you to go on a trip just for those...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We should contribute to making the macarons, too! Don't worry, we cook out in the wild all the time, so {M#he}{F#she} should have some stuff on hand.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, that's great! Then I'll leave the ingredient gathering to you. As long as we have some sweet flowers and wheat, I can start the baking.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Then I'll go look for some boxes nearby, for a makeshift table and chairs.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Great, then I'll prep the stove. Let's get to work, everyone!

talks.objective: Give the Wheat and Sweet Flower to Navia

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did you find the ingredients?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You've all done your part! Just leave the rest to me.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Navia bakes a batch of macarons with her usual gusto.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, these macarons look and taste macanificent! Your cooking is as good as ever, Navia!

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Boss's baking skills have always been famous. Everyone in the Spina knows how exceptionally talented she is.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's just a hobby. There's no need to praise me for it like that.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Have you two seriously never considered joining us? You're so close to the Boss, and she obviously trusts you with all her heart, so...

choices.text: There are still some important things we must do.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I see... Is that why you have to always stay on the road?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, you just happened to walk in on our little reunion. It's actually been quite a while since we last spent time together.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Adventurers never stay in one place for long. The name of Spina di Rosula would just tie them down.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Besides, after everything we've been through together, I'm sure our hearts would remain intertwined even if we found ourselves on opposite sides of the world!

choices.text: Navia's right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if Paimon was far beyond the horizon, she'd still remember the delicious taste of Navia's macarons!

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I understand now. Then I am very lucky indeed to have been graced with the chance to meet the two of you.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I will endeavor to make the most of this short yet fortuitous encounter, and enjoy every moment we spend together.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We've got no wine with us, but let's still toast with water! In celebration of this moment!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I thought I heard something just now. Was it just some small critter?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cheers! Hey, what are you doing? Quick, join in on the toast!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Cheers!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: May your travels go smoothly, may the Spina continue to grow, and may our friendship last until the end of time!

choices.text: That's certainly one way of putting it...
You really wanna poach me from the Adventurers' Guild, huh?

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Hahaha, was it that obvious? I just thought you would be a great fit, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, if it isn't my dear partners!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That voice... It's Navia!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, I didn't expect to run into you guys here today. Are you headed somewhere?

choices.text: Just getting our daily dose of adventuring in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How about you, Navia? Are you still busy rebuilding Poisson?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah, there are still tons of issues to fix. It certainly hasn't been easy.

choices.text: No plans in particular.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: #Boss, you're back! {NICKNAME} and Paimon, welcome back to Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh hey! Fancy seeing you again, Florent! Is it your turn to take care of Navia now?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey, I can totally take care of myself! For the time being, I'll go around without any attendants.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We did hand over some of Melus' old responsibilities to Florent, though. It's been really nice to have him around to help out.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Thank you for the compliment, Boss.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: As you see, I've been working closely with the Boss on rebuilding Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Mr. Melus was an extremely capable and respected member of the Spina. I've got some really big shoes to fill.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, there's no need to be so formal. Everyone's practically old friends by now.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Were you waiting here for me? Did we manage to make any progress on the statue?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Yeah, we contacted a sculptor about the job, but they can't get started on sourcing a correctly sized block without knowing the design that we want to use first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're commissioning a statue?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah, so basically, we've been meaning to commission a statue of my parents in commemoration of everything they've done for the Spina and the town of Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But since my father was known as "Callas the Unfaithful" for the longest time, it would have been too controversial to commission a statue of him.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But now that his name has been cleared, and the town is also being rebuilt, I thought this would be the perfect chance to actually realize this dream.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: The funds to build the statue were freely donated by the people of Poisson, to show their appreciation for Ms. Clementine and Mr. Callas and everything they did.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shouldn't Navia be featured with them, too?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Me? I'm just the newbie President that's running around and causing everyone trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Maybe we can have this conversation again in a few decades, once I've done more for the town and the people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, there's no need to be so humble! Didn't you just help save the entire country?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: I agree wholeheartedly. I also believe that Boss should have a place on the statue.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey, if you keep inflating my ego like this, I might just float off into the sky with my parasol.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Haha, just kidding! There's no way that I'd accept that kind of compliment at face value. At a minimum, I'd have to match what my father did for the people.

choices.text: Well, if that's what you think...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, thanks for the vote of confidence! I just don't think I'm ready yet.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, Florent, now it's up to us to confirm the final design, right?

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Mhm. We can ask the sculptor to start looking for a good block once we've decided on the poses for Ms. Clementine and Mr. Callas.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: But we haven't had any real discussions yet on the possible designs. I feel like I should get a few promising designs first, and then send them over to you to review...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Eh, there's no need for all that. Let's decide on a design right now!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, come over here with me.

choices.text: Me?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Modeling a few poses, of course! Here, just pretend to be Callas, and I'll be Clementine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's, um...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Didn't you say on the boat that Callas and Clementine sounded like great partners? Well, then there's no one better to fill this role than my most valuable partner!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Florent, let's grab some reference shots!

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: You've got it, Boss. I'll go get the Kamera.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, what do you think? Got any ideas?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uhh, shouldn't you be running this show?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, I've actually discussed it a bit with Florent before, but I could never come up with any fresh or original ideas... It's probably because my idea of them is already kind of set in stone.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So I want to pick your brain for a bit, and see if you can come up with some new and interesting ideas.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: I'm all good here, Boss. Feel free to start posing whenever.

choices.text: Okay, then let's try for something... imposing.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Imposing, huh... Oh, I've got it! Let's try this!

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: This pose... It makes me recall Spina di Rosula's glorious golden age.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But isn't Clementine's pose a bit too... bold and heroic? Was she really that kind of person?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we were to stick with this pose, maybe people would wonder if she was actually the real boss behind the scenes.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Well, tabloids did indeed speculate as much back in the day. But the Spina pulled a few strings, and made both the report and the journalist disappear...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon was just kidding! Please don't make Paimon disappear!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, what Florent meant was that we asked the journalist to choose a new alias.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You're right, though, that this may not accurately represent the image of her in our hearts. Let's try to come up with something else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, we tried a bunch of different ideas, but none of them felt right. Paimon's all out of brain juice, now, too...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, don't worry, we still got a lot of reference shots out of the session, and each of them can be considered to be a souvenir in their own right. Let's just keep the ideas we tried as backups.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Man, if I knew I was going to do a photoshoot with {NICKNAME}, I would have prepared a lot of outfits and props ahead of time...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, outfits... Ah! That's the errand I forgot back in the city! Do either of you still remember that girl? The girl I went to see with you two. Her name is Adele.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon remembers her! She was the one that we met while investigating Mr. Callas' case, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She always believed that her father, Jacques, was a good person.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yes, that's exactly who I'm talking about! So, after the case, she was finally willing to talk to me, and she told me that she wanted to join the Spina too.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I said that it's fine, but young children are not allowed to join the Spina. She will just have to wait a few years, and then we'll welcome her with open arms. Since she's still a child, though, she thought I was just trying to let her down gently...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But how could I get her to believe that I meant what I said? In the end, I came up with an idea. I'd have a Spina uniform made, and give it to her as a gift.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But I got so busy and distracted in the city that I forgot to pick the uniform up... Ugh, so I did forget something important after all.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Don't worry, Boss. I can send someone to pick it up right away.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: On the matter of the statue, we should still come up with a few more ideas for the design. I'll have to trouble you to source some for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We could have just done that from the start...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hey, at least this way, we got some cool pictures.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right... They'll have some value as souvenirs, at least.

choices.text: Okay, then let's try... looking out into the distance.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ah, by that... do you mean as if we were standing on a boat and looking out at the sea? Sure, let's give that a try!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, you really remind Paimon of a captain and their first mate!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Look over there, my dear Clementine. As you can see, every tree on that island is dripping with Mora fruit."

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Hmm... But there's something off with the composition. This pose makes Mr. Callas look too tall next to the lady.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, I see what you mean. Then let's swap.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon is a fan! A statue like this would look fantastic on a boat.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wait, but we can't do that. Very few people would see the statue if we were to put it on a boat. This statue is meant to be placed in the town.

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: But then, since we're putting it in the town, the whole point of the pose would be lost.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, okay... We'll try to think of something else...

choices.text: Okay, then why don't we just strike a happy pose?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: A... happy pose? You mean, something like... we were laughing together at a funny joke?

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Huh, would all that be able to come through with just a picture?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Would we even be able to tell what they're supposed to be laughing about?

response.speaker: Florent
response.text: Yeah, and that'd probably be a massive pain to sculpt as well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm, could one of you try striking a pose like you're talking, while the other one laughs?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Er, that actually sounds pretty hard to pull off. Forget it, let's try something else.

choices.text: What are you doing?
I think it'll just be a matter of time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, if it isn't my dear partners!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That voice... It's Navia!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, I didn't expect to run into you guys here today. Are you headed somewhere?

choices.text: Just getting our daily dose of adventuring in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How about you, Navia? Are you still busy rebuilding Poisson?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Heh, we've wrapped up most of the rebuilding, but there are still a few things left to take care of.

choices.text: No plans in particular.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we not taking the boat this time?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's nice to walk from time to time, isn't it? Think of it as something like a hiking trip.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Once we're there, we can stay a few days before we return.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Sounds good... I haven't walked this road in a long time.
